Task 7 review: implementation approved — faithful to the brief, both forced deviations verified correct, dead code fully removed, and the two hardest decisions (once-captured snapshot, seed-vs-converge asymmetry) implemented exactly right and genuinely pinned. The reviewer independently re-derived your fatal-vs-survivable and audit-shape mutations and confirmed both; it called the fatal-vs-survivable test the strongest in the file.

Seven items. One is a shipped-code defect; the rest are coverage.

**IMPORTANT 1 — your Adopted-half assertion has no teeth, and it is the one mutation missing from your table.**
`bootstrap.rs:329-338`. The fixture is `Adopted { content_changed: false, previous_content: None }`. Mutate `:106` from `if *content_changed {` to `if true {` — the natural mutation for that guard — and the test stays green, because the inner `if let Some(previous)` at `:108` sees `None` and skips the audit anyway. So the `content_changed` guard on the audit path is currently unfalsifiable. Your report claims this half is mutation-provable; it isn't.
Fix: either add a case with `Adopted { content_changed: false, previous_content: Some(..) }` — an impossible state per the classifier, which is exactly what a defensive guard is for — or drop the redundant `content_changed` guard and let `if let Some` carry the decision alone. Your call; say which you chose and why.

**IMPORTANT 2 — the char-boundary walk-back is untested; deleting `:57-60` passes the whole suite.**
Your only oversized fixture is `"x".repeat(MAX + 500)` — pure ASCII, so `is_char_boundary(8192)` is true immediately and the loop body never runs. Real failure: a tampered row containing multi-byte text (an accented char or smart quote in a Cedar comment) over 8 KiB with byte 8192 landing mid-character → `source[..end]` panics inside `AppState::new` and the replica dies before serving. The shipped code is correct; the arithmetic just has no guard.
Fix: add a multi-byte fixture, e.g. `"é".repeat(MAX/2 + 10)`, asserting the result is `<= MAX` bytes and is a prefix of the input. Note your existing `assert_eq!(src.len(), MAX)` cannot be reused — the truncation lands below the cap when it walks back.

**IMPORTANT 3 — the only shipped-code defect: a failed `existing_policy_ids()` read is swallowed, and the resulting fatal log actively misleads.**
`bootstrap.rs:71` + `:88`. A connection blip during boot against a healthy database holding all nine rows → `Err` → `unwrap_or_default()` → empty snapshot → the next reconcile failure takes the FATAL arm → the replica exits logging *"failed to seed a missing starter policy; refusing to boot with an incomplete policy set"* about a policy that exists, with no trace of why. On-call is told the policy set is incomplete when it is intact, and may reach for destructive remediation.
Fix: keep the fail-closed fallback (that direction is correct per spec), but replace `unwrap_or_default()` with a `match` that logs `tracing::warn!(error = %err, ...)` explaining that the snapshot was unreadable and every failure this boot will therefore be treated as fatal. Also extend the fake so `existing_policy_ids` can be made to fail, and add a test that the degradation happens and is logged-not-silent.

**IMPORTANT 4 — the orphan branches are entirely untested.**
`bootstrap.rs:126-132` and `:190-192`. `ScriptedPolicies.orphans` is declared and read but no test ever populates it, and `ScriptedRoles::orphaned_system_role_keys` is hardcoded `vec![]`. Requirement 7's real invariant — *no audit row per orphan per replica per boot*, on an append-only table — has zero guard: adding an audit write to the orphan branch ships green today. Use the field you already have; assert both that orphans are counted/logged and that the audit buffer stays empty.

**MINOR 5 — the extra test's comment describes an impossible failure mode.** `bootstrap.rs:409-411` says re-reading per policy "would let a row this boot just seeded make a LATER failure on a still-missing row look survivable." The guard at `:78` compares against the failing doc's OWN id, so seeding A can never change B's classification. The hoist is a cost/determinism decision (9 full-table reads → 1, one consistent basis), not a correctness one. Keep the test, fix the comment.

**MINOR 6 — assert the two remaining `detail` keys.** `bootstrap.rs:300-308` asserts three of the five documented keys; `policy_id` and `content_changed` are unasserted, so dropping either reddens nothing. Add both.

**MINOR 7 — cap `previous.description` too.** `:165` copies it unbounded while `source` is capped at `:164`. The cap's own doc justifies itself as "attacker-influenced text landing in an append-only table" — the description comes from the same externally-modified row and is equally attacker-controlled. Apply the same truncation helper to it. This extends the brief rather than contradicting it; I'm authorizing it.

Mutation-verify I-1, I-2, and I-4 before reporting, and `touch` after each swap to dodge the stale-binary trap. Report the covering test files, the commands, and their output. Append to the same report file. Foreground only.
